The Famvan Is a Comfort-Maximizing Camper Van Made for Family Adventures, It's Now for Sale
36 photos
Photo: Beachside Custom Vans
A lot of people who travel by camper van would like to bring their family along on the adventures, but not all have such a comfort-maximizing setup like the one I'd like to share with you today. Meet the Famvan.
The Famvan is a project based on a 2025 AWD Mercedes-Benz Sprinter with a 170" wheelbase. It was created by Beachside Custom Vans, a Jacksonville, Florida-based company specializing in designing and building premium camper vans.
This build was made for a customer with a family of four who didn't end up using it as much as they planned. In fact, it was barely used, and they decided to list it for sale – more info about that at the end of the article.
As always, let's first take a look at the van's exterior. For starters, the van rides on Black Rhino wheels wrapped in BFGoodrich KO3 all-terrain tires.
Beachside Custom Vans went further in upgrading the off-roading capabilities by installing Bilstein struts and an Agile Offroad Premium RIP kit - its key components are front and rear shocks and a custom-rated rear leaf spring pack.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Beachside Custom Vans At the rear, you'll come across an Owl Vans spare tire carrier / ladder combo. Use it to climb on the van, and you'll find an FVC (Flatline Van Co.) Safari rack.
The rack holds five front-facing Baja Designs LP9 Pro light pods (three clear and two amber), a Fiamma F45S awning, and offers a ton of space for attaching gear. You can also use it as a roof deck. What's more, it has two cut-outs for a vent fan and an A/C unit.
Other notable mods are AMP Research powered side steps, AM Auto opening windows with screens, FVC rocker lockers, an ARB air compressor with two connections in the front and back, and power and water hookups. Moreover, Owl Vans hood gas struts make it easier for you to open the hood.
Enter, and a bright, welcoming interior will greet you. The customer opted for an eye-catching design consisting of a mix of white and grain-finished cabinetry, a slatted white oak ceiling with recessed LED light strips, and walls finished with grey woven fabric.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Beachside Custom Vans The look is complemented by white solid surface countertops, some black accents, like the cabinet and drawer handles, and soft blue faux leather couch upholstery.
The interior has an open layout, with no wall separating the driver's cabin from the living space. This setup lets you turn the cabin into a seating area after you've parked the van.
Thanks to their factory swivel bases, the driver and passenger seats can be turned around to face the back of the van. What's more, the builders added a White Top Adventures overhead cab shelf above.
Straight ahead of the entrance, you'll come across a continuation of the front seating area. Beachside Custom Vans fitted two captain's chairs complete with armrests and seatbelts, as well as a Lagun table mount.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Beachside Custom Vans Next, we have the kitchen on the passenger side. It features a deep stainless steel sink with a cover, a portable stove, and a flip-up table for additional counter space.
Two overhead cabinets, four drawers, and a cabinet underneath the sink are available for storage in the kitchen. But you can use even more space in a massive unit on the opposite side.
Besides integrating a Dometic NRX 115 fridge with a tiny freezer compartment, it offers two large closets, two medium-sized drawers, and a large drawer. The latter has heavy-duty slides that hold a Laveo dry-flush toilet.
Finally, most of the time spent in this van (except for when driving) will be spent in the back. Beachside Custom Vans came up with a space-maximizing setup that can be used for both lounging and sleeping.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Beachside Custom Vans During the day, you can spend some time in the lower part of the area, where you'll find two long benches with two large tables in the middle. This is the hang-out spot, perfect for accommodating a large group of people for dinner, playing board games, and more.
You can transform the setup into a sleeping arrangement quite easily and quickly. To do that, you must remove the tabletops, attach them in between the benches to connect them, and rearrange the cushions. The result is a huge bed that can easily accommodate two adults.
However, this isn't the main sleeping arrangement. Above the lounge area, you'll notice what looks like a lower ceiling. It's, in fact, the lower part of an elevator bed that's made to perfectly resemble the ceiling.
At the flip of a switch, you can lower the elevator bed to your preferred height. You can even leave enough space underneath it to create a bunk bed setup to accommodate four people.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Beachside Custom Vans The lounge area sits a bit higher than the rest of the living space. Beachside Custom Vans used the extra height to install a surprisingly long drawer that can be pulled out toward the rear of the van. You'll also notice extra storage space in the form of Van Essential bags attached to the rear doors.
The two benches I mentioned earlier accommodate the utility systems. Power is on the passenger side – the electrical system's highlights are an 800 Ah battery bank paired with a 3,000 W inverter.
You can use three charging sources to keep the batteries topped off: solar power , shore power, and DC-DC charging while the engine is running.
As for plumbing, the van is equipped with a 35-gallon (132-liter) freshwater tank, an 11-gallon (41-liter) greywater tank, a water filtration system, a 4-gallon (15-liter) Bosch water heater, and an outdoor shower with a quick connect fitting.
Photo: Beachside Custom Vans You can rest assured that all-season adventures are possible with this camper van. This is possible thanks to the double 3M Thinsulate insulation and two important systems: a diesel-powered Espar heater that's tapped into the vehicle's fuel tank, and a 12V A/C unit above the kitchen.
The kitchen's backsplash integrates the "command center" for the rig's utilities. It includes three dimmer light switches, a thermostat, charging points, a battery monitor, and switches for the water pump, the electric dump valves for the water tanks, and the elevator bed.
All in all, Beachside Custom Vans took a plain AWD Sprinter van and turned it into a family-friendly home on wheels packed full with luxuries, ready for any adventure you throw at it.
As mentioned initially, the Famvan is looking for a new owner – it's barely used, with its odometer reading just 4,000 miles (6,437 km). According to the company's listing , the asking price is $205,000 (€182,825) – that's about right given the price of an AWD Sprinter platform and all the modifications and additions it has.
